title: Latency-aware deferred prefilter sampler and perf-regression guardrail
creator: Priya Khatri
description:
Summary:
We need a low-cost, latency-aware sampling layer that moves as much decision logic off the hot path as possible while preserving the ability to capture tail events and performance regressions. This ticket implements a deferred prefilter that emits a tiny sampling hint at ingress, defers full sampling decisions to a background worker when safe, and introduces guardrails to prevent perf regressions during rollout.

What we're building:
- Ingress prefilter: lightweight C++/Go path that computes a 1-byte hint (probabilistic score + TTL) using request headers, route metadata, and a tiny LRU for recent error spikes. This runs inline and must stay allocation-free.
- Deferred decision worker: background component consumes enriched request traces (minimal header + KV pointers) and performs more expensive checks (tail-based heuristics, anomaly detectors, content-aware Bloom filters) before committing a full trace.
- Latency-aware gating: if request latency is above a per-route SLO threshold, we bias toward keeping the trace; if below, we downsample aggressively.
- Perf-regression guardrail: built-in canary rollout that monitors hotpath p50/p95 CPU and allocation changes; automatic rollback if metrics exceed thresholds for 10m.
- Observability & dashboards: new tracing metric series (prefilter_rate, deferred_commit_rate, deferred_latency_ms, hotpath_alloc_delta) and a dashboard tile on latency/error dashboard with regression alerts and runbook links.

Progress updates:
- 2026-03-10: Proposal doc posted: https://confluence.internal.redwood/obs/deferred-prefilter-sampler (draft).
- 2026-03-11: Prototype prefilter implemented in platform/ingress: small Go module using object pool; microbenchmarks show <120ns median overhead. Benchmark: https://perf.redwood/internal/bench/ENG-112357.
- 2026-03-12: Background worker prototype finished. It currently communicates via a bounded channel and a redis-backed buffer for overflow. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7123.
- 2026-03-13: End-to-end integration test added to CI (integration/telemetry-smoke). Initial run passed but we observed a 2% p95 CPU increase on canary; temporary flags added to throttle deferred commit concurrency.
- 2026-03-14: Design review feedback applied (see comments below). Preparing canary rollout to 5% of traffic.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Why prefilter hint vs full decision inline: we trade richer decision logic for minimal hotpath overhead. Prefilter reduces allocations and keeps the critical path deterministic.
- Bounded buffer + background worker vs synchronous sampling: background worker avoids blocking the request but requires careful overflow/backpressure handling; we choose a redis-backed overflow with leaky consumption to preserve durability.
- Latency-aware biasing: risk that latency signal is noisy; mitigate with short-term EWMA smoothing per route.
- Tail event capture: full tail-sampling still supported by the background worker using a reservoir sampler that prioritizes high-latency traces.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before rollout to 100%):
- Hotpath overhead <= +0.5% p50 CPU and +1% p95 CPU on representative canary (compared to baseline).
- Added allocations on hotpath < 64 bytes/request.
- deferred_commit_rate metric present and matches sampling targets within 5%.
- End-to-end test coverage: synthetic tail injection test that proves we capture 95% of simulated tail anomalies at configured sampling ratios.
- Dashboard and alerting configured: regression alert triggers if hotpath_alloc_delta > 128 bytes or p95 CPU increases > 5% for 10m.

Implementation notes for engineers:
- Hotpath implementation should avoid map allocations; use sync.Pool for hint objects. Language: Go for ingress, Rust/Go allowed for worker.
- Hint schema: 8-bit struct encoded as a hex header X-RW-SAMP-HINT. Contains: 2-bit version, 3-bit probabilistic score (0-7), 1-bit tail-candidate flag, 2-bit reserved.
- Backpressure: when redis buffer > 90th percentile size we should mark hint TTL=short and allow best-effort sampling to drop to zero for low-latency routes.
- Telemetry: emit counters for prefilter_evals, prefilter_hits, deferred_enqueued, deferred_committed, deferred_dropped, overflow_backpressure_triggered.

Testing plan:
- Microbenchmarks for ingress with benchmark harness: goal median <200ns.
- Load test: simulate 50k RPS of mixed routes with tail anomalies injected; measure capture rate and CPU/alloc delta.
- Chaos scenario: redis latency spikes; verify safe degradation (background worker fallback to in-memory reservoir for limited capacity).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: hidden allocations creep into hotpath. Mitigation: strict code review checklist and CI hotpath allocation test (heapcheck).
- Risk: tail-candidate misclassification reduces observability. Mitigation: default conservative thresholds and rollout at 5% then 25%.
- Risk: background worker overload causing delayed commits. Mitigation: backpressure and prioritized reservoir for tail events.

Follow-ups / open tasks:
- ENG-112400: Add eBPF-based low-overhead error detector as an optional hint source (spike detection at kernel level).
- ENG-112410: Add per-tenant adaptive budgets for deferred commits (billing/telemetry integration).
- UX: dashboard tile and runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1984.

Review feedback (selected):
- PM (Lena Morris): prefer conservative default sampling to avoid noise in evals; agreed and lowered default to 0.5% deferred for low-latency routes.
- Design (Marta Singh): asked to document hint schema versioning; added version field and backward compatibility plan.
- Eng infra (Omar Chen): requested rate-limited redis writes; implemented buffering and batching in PR.

Next steps:
- Merge prototype PR after adding heapcheck and canary rollout script (owner: Diego).
- Run 5% canary for 72 hours, collect hotpath metrics and deferred capture rates.
- If metrics within guardrails, expand to 25% then 100% with automated checks at each stage.
